Wire Input and Expected to the outside of the box. Inside, wire Each step to both backward cards, then connect Assumption box to ① and Cite a given to ②. Wire the join to the box’s inner result port.
qed/level.try-backtracking.title: Trial · Backtracking search
qed/level.try-direct-backward.after: Each \mark{backward} card applies a proof rule directly to the current goal. Its output can feed the next tactic card.
qed/level.try-direct-backward.intro.0.t: A card marked \mark{backward} takes a proof state directly. \mark{backward} Assumption box adds the condition of an implication to the givens. \mark{backward} Cite a given closes a goal that matches a given.
qed/level.try-direct-backward.tasks.try-: Prove each case using cards marked \mark{backward}.
Start with \mark{backward} Assumption box, then finish with \mark{backward} Cite a given.
qed/level.try-direct-backward.title: Try direct rule cards
qed/level.try-direct-rewrite.after: The double-negation law can rewrite inside a formula. In these cases it removes the double negation and leaves the surrounding formula intact.
qed/level.try-direct-rewrite.intro.0.t: A card marked \mark{rewrite} rewrites a proof state directly. Pick a direction on \mark{rewrite} Double negation and see how it rewrites one part of a larger formula.
qed/level.try-direct-rewrite.tasks.try-d: Use a card marked \mark{rewrite} to remove the double negation in each goal.
Choose the rule that turns \(\lnot \lnot A\) into A.
qed/level.try-direct-rewrite.title: Try direct rewrite cards
qed/level.twice.intro.0.t: “\(\text{it rains}\to (\text{it rains}\to \text{the ground is wet})\)” states the condition “it rains” twice. Surely once is enough.
qed/level.twice.tasks.twice.hint.0: The goal is “if it rains, then …”.
qed/level.twice.tasks.twice.hint.1: How many times can an assumption in a box be used?
qed/level.twice.title: The same condition twice
qed/level.u-barber.after: This kind of argument is the <wiki-ref to="qed/diagonal"></wiki-ref>.
qed/level.u-barber.intro.0.t: When a goal follows, the saturator reaches \mark{bottom} sooner or later; when it does not, the saturator may never stop. Is there a machine that can say, for every goal, whether it follows? This topic starts from <part-ref to="lemma:qed/liar"></part-ref> in <level-ref to="qed/kk-one"></level-ref>.
qed/level.u-barber.tasks.u-barber.brief: The village barber says: “I shave exactly those who do not shave themselves.” Given “\(\text{there is an x such that for every y},x\; \text{shaves y}\leftrightarrow y\; \text{does not shave himself}\)”, prove the contradiction \mark{bottom}.
qed/level.u-barber.title: The barber
qed/level.u-cantor.after: This is Cantor’s theorem: a set always has more subsets than elements.
qed/level.u-cantor.tasks.u-cantor.brief: f gives each x a set f(x). Every set is some f(x) (f is onto); and there is a set z holding exactly the y not in f(y). Get the contradiction \mark{bottom}.
qed/level.u-cantor.tasks.u-cantor.hint.0: Take out z first, then the x whose f(x) is z.
qed/level.u-cantor.tasks.u-cantor.hint.1: Taking y = x in both gives \(X\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(Y\leftrightarrow \lnot X\).
qed/level.u-cantor.tasks.u-cantor.hint.2: From these two, build what <part-ref to="lemma:qed/liar"></part-ref> needs.
qed/level.u-cantor.title: Cantor
qed/level.u-halt.after: Passing from one problem to another is a <wiki-ref to="qed/reduction"></wiki-ref>. Provability in first-order logic shows the same <wiki-ref to="qed/undecidable"></wiki-ref>: no program can say, for every goal, whether it follows.
qed/level.u-halt.tasks.u-halt.brief: Given: if some machine decides halting, a machine x can be built that halts on ⟨y⟩ exactly when y does not halt on ⟨y⟩; and if some machine decides A_TM, one deciding halting can be built. Prove no machine decides A_TM.
qed/level.u-halt.tasks.u-halt.hint.0: Assume a machine that decides A_TM.
qed/level.u-halt.tasks.u-halt.hint.1: In the end, a machine still reads its own code.
qed/level.u-halt.title: The halting problem
qed/level.u-ls.tasks.u-ls.brief: ⟨y⟩ is the code of the Turing machine y. L_s holds the codes of machines that do not accept their own code. Supposing some machine x recognises L_s, get the contradiction \mark{bottom}.
qed/level.u-ls.tasks.u-ls.hint.0: Let x read its own code.
qed/level.u-ls.title: Programs that reject themselves
qed/level.x-chain.after: Any box can be traded for K, S and Apply: the <wiki-ref to="qed/deduction"></wiki-ref>.
qed/level.x-chain.tasks.x-chain.hint.0: What does the proof look like with a box? Without one, what does each step inside it?
qed/level.x-chain.tasks.x-chain.hint.1: The Apply inside the box happens under the condition “it rains”.
qed/level.x-chain.title: Joining without a box
qed/level.x-k.intro.0.t: This topic takes the box away, leaving Apply and the K and S you proved. Early provers were like this: one rule, and every other starting point an <wiki-ref to="qed/axiom"></wiki-ref>. Such a prover is a <wiki-ref to="qed/hilbert"></wiki-ref>.
qed/level.x-k.tasks.x-k-2.hint.0: Apply under a condition is what S does.
qed/level.x-k.tasks.x-k-2.hint.1: S’s three sentences need not each be a single word.
qed/level.x-k.tasks.x-k-2.step: Under a condition without a box
qed/level.x-k.title: Without the box: K and S
qed/level.x-merge.tasks.x-merge.hint.0: Which S can the given go into?
qed/level.x-merge.tasks.x-merge.hint.1: After S is applied to the given, what is still missing? You assembled it in <level-ref to="qed/x-self"></level-ref>.
qed/level.x-merge.title: Merging without a box
qed/level.x-self.tasks.x-self.hint.0: Start from S: what does it give after two Applies?
qed/level.x-self.tasks.x-self.hint.1: S’s second sentence need not be a single word. Both sentences S then needs can be made with K.
qed/level.x-self.title: Identity without a box
qed/level.x-swap.tasks.x-swap.hint.0: Which S can the given go into, and what does Apply then give?
qed/level.x-swap.tasks.x-swap.hint.1: Can K supply the missing part? Once two parts meet end to end, join them as in <level-ref to="qed/x-chain"></level-ref>.
qed/level.x-swap.title: Reordering without a box
qed/part.allE.desc: Connect \mark{forall}x. P(x) and choose an object t to obtain P(t).
qed/part.allE.name: Choose an instance
qed/part.allE.settings.t.label: Which thing
qed/part.allI.desc: Name an arbitrary object a on the part. Prove P(a) inside the box and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain \mark{forall}x. P(x) outside. a must not occur in any open assumption.
qed/part.allI.name: For-any box
qed/part.allI.regions.0.label: Inside
qed/part.allI.settings.x.label: Name
qed/part.andE.desc: Connect A \mark{and} B to get A and B at separate outputs.
qed/part.andE.name: Split
qed/part.andE.revisions.0.desc: Connect A \mark{and} B to get A and B at separate outputs. A \mark{iff} B means (A \mark{implies} B) \mark{and} (B \mark{implies} A) and can be split in the same way.
qed/part.andI.desc: Connect A and B to get A \mark{and} B.
qed/part.andI.name: Join
qed/part.anyR.name: Any conclusion
qed/part.append.desc: Connect the results of different proof routes. Continue with the first route that can still proceed, in numbered order.
qed/part.append.name: Join candidates
qed/part.append.revisions.0.desc: Keep every result that can still proceed, in route order, for later steps to check.
qed/part.append.settings.ways.label: Routes
qed/part.arrow.desc: Two shapes switched on the part: from \(A\to B\), gives \(\lnot A\lor B\); from \(\lnot A\lor B\), gives \(A\to B\).
qed/part.arrow.name: Arrow away
qed/part.arrow.revisions.0.desc: Two shapes switched on the part: from \(A\to B\), gives \(\lnot A\lor B\); from \(\lnot A\lor B\), gives \(A\to B\). Each shape is also a rewrite rule.
qed/part.auto.desc: Searches depth first until done: each step tries Assumption, then Goal apart, then Use a given; a path back to an earlier state is not followed.
qed/part.auto.name: Your own auto (Legacy)
qed/part.axK.desc: Choose two sentences A and B on the part; gives A \mark{implies} (B \mark{implies} A).
qed/part.axK.settings.A.label: First
qed/part.axK.settings.B.label: Second
qed/part.axS.desc: Choose three sentences A, B and C on the part; gives (A \mark{implies} (B \mark{implies} C)) \mark{implies} ((A \mark{implies} B) \mark{implies} (A \mark{implies} C)).
qed/part.axS.settings.A.label: First
qed/part.axS.settings.B.label: Second
qed/part.axS.settings.C.label: Third
qed/part.botE.desc: From the contradiction \mark{bottom}, gives whatever sentence is chosen on the part.
qed/part.botE.name: Explosion
qed/part.botE.settings.C.label: Conclude
qed/part.chain.desc: From A \mark{implies} B and B \mark{implies} C, gives A \mark{implies} C.
qed/part.chain.name: Chain
qed/part.clausify.desc: Adds the negated goal to the hypotheses, brings them to CNF, removes the \mark{exists}s and splits them into clauses.
qed/part.clausify.name: Into clauses, all the way (Legacy)
qed/part.consFront.desc: Puts “This” at the front of “A list”; when what comes into “A list” is not a list, makes a list of the two.
qed/part.consFront.inputs.0.label: This
qed/part.consFront.inputs.1.label: A list
qed/part.consFront.name: Put first
qed/part.defer.desc: Moves the first goal to the end; the second becomes the first.
qed/part.defer.name: Defer
qed/part.dist.desc: “Or” distributed over “and”, four shapes switched on the part: \(A\lor (B\land C)\) and \((A\lor B)\land (A\lor C)\) give each other, and so do \((A\land B)\lor C\) and \((A\lor C)\land (B\lor C)\).
qed/part.dist.name: Distribute
qed/part.dist.revisions.0.desc: “Or” distributed over “and”, four shapes switched on the part: \(A\lor (B\land C)\) and \((A\lor B)\land (A\lor C)\) give each other, and so do \((A\land B)\lor C\) and \((A\lor C)\land (B\lor C)\). Each shape is also a rewrite rule.
qed/part.dm.desc: A negation trades “or” for “and” and back, four shapes switched on the part: \(\lnot (A\lor B)\) and \(\lnot A\land \lnot B\) give each other, and so do \(\lnot (A\land B)\) and \(\lnot A\lor \lnot B\).
qed/part.dm.name: De Morgan
qed/part.dm.revisions.0.desc: A negation trades “or” for “and”, “there is” for “for all”, and back: eight shapes switched on the part.
qed/part.dneg.desc: Two shapes switched on the part: from \(\lnot \lnot A\), gives \(A\); from \(A\), gives \(\lnot \lnot A\).
qed/part.dneg.name: Double negation
qed/part.dneg.revisions.0.desc: Two shapes switched on the part: from \(\lnot \lnot A\), gives \(A\); from \(A\), gives \(\lnot \lnot A\). Each shape is also a rewrite rule.
qed/part.each.desc: The parts inside run once on each goal, seeing only that goal each time; if any goal fails, the whole part fails.
qed/part.each.name: Each goal in turn
qed/part.each.regions.0.label: Each goal in turn
qed/part.eachOf.desc: Wire in a list: the frame receives one item at a time, and its inner output goes to “Result”; each item is processed once, and the results form a list in the original order.
qed/part.eachOf.name: For each
qed/part.eachOf.regions.0.label: Each item
qed/part.elimGen.desc: Wire in a declaration (the declared sentence and its list of introduction rules); gives the declaration’s elimination rule.
qed/part.elimGen.name: The elimination rule generator
qed/part.elimRules.desc: Applies every elimination rule to the hypotheses: Split, Case analysis, applying an “if”, Explosion, the instance box, and choose an instance then use it. Each fit gives one result.
qed/part.elimRules.name: Use a given (Legacy)
qed/part.erule.desc: Takes rules: the rule’s conclusion is unified with the first goal and its first premise with one of that goal’s hypotheses; the goal is replaced by the remaining premises, one goal each. Given several rules, it uses the first that applies.
qed/part.erule.name: A rule, then a given (Legacy)
qed/part.erule.revisions.0.desc: Takes rules: the rule’s conclusion is unified with the first goal and its first premise with one of that goal’s hypotheses; the goal is replaced by the remaining premises, one goal each. Each rule wired in, and each hypothesis that fits, gives one result.
qed/part.exE.desc: Connect \mark{exists}x. P(x) and name the existing object a on the part. Inside the box, P(a) may be assumed. Prove C and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain C outside. a must not appear in C or in any open assumption.
qed/part.exE.name: Witness box
qed/part.exE.regions.0.label: Inside
qed/part.exE.settings.x.label: Witness
qed/part.exI.desc: Connect P(t) to obtain \mark{exists}x. P(x), with t as a witness. If exactly one existential statement fits, it is selected automatically; if several fit, choose the conclusion on the part.
qed/part.exI.name: Generalise
qed/part.exI.settings.target.label: Conclusion to derive
qed/part.frule.desc: Takes rules: the rule’s first premise is unified with one of the first goal’s hypotheses and its conclusion is added to the hypotheses; each remaining premise becomes a goal, placed first. Given several rules, it uses the first that applies.
qed/part.frule.name: One step forward (Legacy)
qed/part.gAnd.desc: a \mark{and} b: outputs true only when both inputs are true; otherwise false.
qed/part.gAnd.name: And \mark{and}
qed/part.gIff.desc: a \mark{iff} b: outputs true when a and b are both true or both false; false when one is true and the other false.
qed/part.gIff.name: Equivalent \mark{iff}
qed/part.gImp.desc: Outputs false only when a is true and b is false; true otherwise.
qed/part.gImp.name: If…then… \mark{implies}
qed/part.gNot.desc: \mark{not}a: true in gives false out; false in gives true out.
qed/part.gNot.name: Not \mark{not}
qed/part.gOr.desc: Outputs true when at least one input is true; false when both are false.
qed/part.gOr.name: Or \mark{or}
qed/part.gTrue.desc: The two directions of If–then joined by Or. The output is true for every pair of inputs.
qed/part.gTrue.name: Always True
qed/part.iff.desc: Two shapes switched on the part: from \(A\leftrightarrow B\), gives \((\lnot A\lor B)\land (\lnot B\lor A)\), and the other way round. Each shape is also a rewrite rule.
qed/part.iff.name: Equivalence away
qed/part.impI.desc: A box, with A set on the part. Inside, A may be used as an assumption; prove B there and wire it to “Conclusion”, and the part gives A \mark{implies} B.
qed/part.impI.name: Assumption box
qed/part.impI.regions.0.label: Inside
qed/part.impI.settings.A.label: Assume
qed/part.introRules.desc: Applies every introduction rule backwards to the first goal: Join, the assumption box, Add alternative left and right, the for-any box, Generalise. Each rule that fits gives one result.
qed/part.introRules.name: Goal apart (Legacy)
qed/part.keepBound.desc: Wire in a rule. If it begins with bound variables (\mark{meta-all}x. …), the frame works on the rule after them, and the output keeps the same bound variables in front; if it has none, the frame works on the input itself.
qed/part.keepBound.name: Keep \mark{meta-all}
qed/part.keepBound.regions.0.label: The rule after the bound variables
qed/part.lem.desc: Choose a sentence A on the part; gives A \mark{or} \mark{not}A.
qed/part.lem.name: Excluded middle
qed/part.liar.name: The liar
qed/part.merge.desc: From A \mark{implies} (A \mark{implies} B), gives A \mark{implies} B.
qed/part.merge.name: Merge
qed/part.metis.desc: Turns the goal into clauses, finds a certificate that reaches \mark{bottom} and has the kernel replay it: if it passes, the goal is closed; if the certificate fails the check, the part fails.
qed/part.metis.name: Reconstructor (Legacy)
qed/part.mkRule.desc: Builds the rule \mark{open-bracket}premises\mark{close-bracket} \mark{entails} conclusion from premises (a list or a single item) and a conclusion. A sentence is a premise as it is; a rule becomes a premise with its own assumptions.
qed/part.mkRule.inputs.0.label: Premises
qed/part.mkRule.inputs.1.label: Conclusion
qed/part.mkRule.name: Make a rule
qed/part.mp.desc: From A \mark{implies} B and A, gives B.
qed/part.mp.name: Apply
qed/part.mp.revisions.0.desc: From A \mark{implies} B and A, gives B. \mark{not}A is A \mark{implies} \mark{bottom}, so from \mark{not}A and A, gives the contradiction \mark{bottom}.
qed/part.orE.desc: Connect A \mark{or} B and assume A and B in separate boxes. When both prove the same C and connect it to their respective “Conclusion” ports, the part outputs C.
qed/part.orE.name: Case analysis
qed/part.orE.regions.0.label: Case one
qed/part.orE.regions.1.label: Case two
qed/part.orI.desc: Connect A and choose another statement B and its position to get A \mark{or} B or B \mark{or} A. B need not be proved.
qed/part.orI.name: Add alternative
qed/part.orI.settings.other.label: Other side
qed/part.orI.settings.side.label: Other side goes
qed/part.oracle.desc: A fast prover: it cancels all complementary literals between two clauses at once, round after round until \mark{bottom} appears or no new clause does. It too records the two parents of each new clause.
qed/part.oracle.name: Someone else’s prover
qed/part.raa.name: By contradiction
qed/part.refl.desc: Choose a thing t on the part; gives t = t.
qed/part.refl.name: Reflexivity
qed/part.refl.settings.t.label: Which thing
qed/part.repeat.desc: The frame receives the input; its inner output goes to “Result” and back into the frame, round after round, until it stops changing, and the last round’s result is given. If a round fails, it stops at the round before.
qed/part.repeat.name: Repeat frame
qed/part.repeat.regions.0.label: Each round
qed/part.repeat.revisions.0.desc: The frame receives the input; its inner output goes to “Result” and back into the frame, round after round, until it stops changing, and the last round’s result is given. If a round fails, it stops at the round before. With several results, it goes on from the first only.
qed/part.replay.desc: When the clause set contains \mark{bottom}, the steps to \mark{bottom} go to the kernel: each input clause used must come from a hypothesis, and each step must be proved from its two parents (variables instantiated by unification) by Own auto. If all pass, the goal the clauses came from is proved; otherwise it names the failing step.
qed/part.replay.name: Replay
qed/part.res.desc: Wire in two clauses, one holding A and the other \mark{not}A, in any position: that pair is cancelled and what is left is joined with “or”; when nothing is left, gives the contradiction \mark{bottom}. One pair at a time.
qed/part.res.name: Resolve
qed/part.resolve.desc: Tries every pair of clauses in the set once: when a literal of one unifies with the complement of a literal of the other, that pair is cancelled and the remaining literals form a new clause, added with a record of its two parents. Tautologies and duplicates are dropped. It can be set to resolve only against one-literal clauses.
qed/part.resolve.name: A round of resolution
qed/part.resolve.settings.unit.label: Cancel with
qed/part.rewrite.desc: Wire in s = t and a sentence containing s; the part marks each s in it, and the ticked ones become t.
qed/part.rewrite.name: Substitute equals
qed/part.rewrite.settings.at.label: Which occurrences to replace
qed/part.rule.desc: Takes rules at its “R” port and uses the first that applies: the first goal is unified with the rule’s conclusion and replaced by its premises (one goal per premise, each premise’s own assumptions added to the hypotheses). Any ?-letter not yet fixed stays in the goals.
qed/part.rule.name: Apply a rule backwards (Legacy)
qed/part.rw.desc: Takes rewrite rules: in the first goal, outside in and left to right, the first place that fits the rule’s left side becomes its right side, that place alone. A rule with conditions adds each as a new goal after this one. Given several, it uses the first that fits; if nothing fits, it fails.
qed/part.rw.inputs.1.label: Rule
qed/part.rw.name: Rewrite (Legacy)
qed/part.rw.revisions.0.desc: Takes rewrite rules: in the first goal, outside in and left to right, the first place that fits the rule’s left side becomes its right side, that place alone. A rule with conditions adds each as a new goal after this one. Given several, it uses the first that fits; if nothing fits, it fails. With “Where” set to the hypotheses, it rewrites the first goal’s first hypothesis from the top that fits.
qed/part.rw.settings.at.label: Where
qed/part.rw.settings.at.options.0.label: Goal
qed/part.rw.settings.at.options.1.label: Hypotheses
qed/part.saturate.desc: Resolves round after round until \mark{bottom} appears or no new clause does.
qed/part.saturate.name: The saturator
qed/part.search.desc: Depth-first search: the parts inside take one step on the state received, then go on from each result; each path is followed to its end before backtracking to the next, until no goal remains. Gives every finished state it finds. A step back to where it was (no fewer goals, no more hypotheses) is not followed. A depth limit can be set on the part.
qed/part.search.name: Backtracking search
qed/part.search.regions.0.label: Each step
qed/part.search.settings.depth.label: At most
qed/part.simp.desc: Takes a list of rewrite rules: each round, the first that fits rewrites one place, round after round, until none fits.
qed/part.simp.name: Simp (Legacy)
qed/part.simp.revisions.0.desc: Takes a list of rewrite rules: each round, the first that fits rewrites one place, round after round, until none fits. With “Where” set to the hypotheses, it rewrites the first goal’s hypotheses.
qed/part.simp.settings.at.label: Where
qed/part.skolem.desc: Removes every \mark{exists} from the first goal’s hypotheses: one with no \mark{forall} outside is taken out as the instance box does; one under a \mark{forall} becomes a new function of all the enclosing \mark{forall} variables (sk1(x) …). The hypotheses must be in negation normal form first.
qed/part.skolem.name: Skolemise
qed/part.swap.desc: From A \mark{implies} (B \mark{implies} C), gives B \mark{implies} (A \mark{implies} C).
qed/part.swap.name: Swap
qed/part.swapConcl.desc: Wire in a rule and a sentence: keeps the rule’s premises and makes the sentence its conclusion.
qed/part.swapConcl.inputs.0.label: Rule
qed/part.swapConcl.inputs.1.label: Becomes
qed/part.swapConcl.name: Swap conclusion
qed/part.toClauses.desc: The first goal must be \mark{bottom}: its hypotheses are split into clauses. Each must be in CNF; conjunctions are split, each disjunction becomes a clause, \mark{forall}s are dropped and variables read as universally quantified.
qed/part.toClauses.name: Extract clauses
qed/part.uCheck.desc: Finds ?A \mark{dot-equals} t where t contains ?A and is not ?A itself, and reports failure.
qed/part.uCheck.name: Occurs check
qed/part.uCheck.revisions.0.desc: Finds ?A \mark{dot-equals} t where ?A cannot be t and reports failure: t contains ?A and is not ?A itself, or t contains a variable bound by the \mark{meta-all} in front.
qed/part.uConflict.desc: Finds an equation with no ?-letter on either side and different structures (an “and” against an “or”, two different sentences …) and reports failure.
qed/part.uConflict.name: Conflict
qed/part.uDecompose.desc: Finds an equation whose sides have the same structure (both “and”, the same predicate …) and splits it into equations between corresponding parts: ?A \mark{and} ?B \mark{dot-equals} it rains \mark{and} it is windy becomes ?A \mark{dot-equals} it rains and ?B \mark{dot-equals} it is windy. \mark{not}A splits as A \mark{implies} \mark{bottom}.
qed/part.uDecompose.name: Decompose
qed/part.uDecompose.revisions.0.desc: Finds an equation whose sides have the same structure and splits it into equations between corresponding parts. When both sides are “for all” (or both “there is”), it takes out the two bodies with one variable x for both, and marks the equation \mark{meta-all}x: x is bound by a quantifier.
qed/part.uDelete.desc: Finds an equation with identical sides, t \mark{dot-equals} t, and deletes it.
qed/part.uDelete.name: Delete
qed/part.uEliminate.desc: Finds ?A \mark{dot-equals} t (t free of ?A) where ?A still occurs in other equations, and replaces ?A with t there.
qed/part.uEliminate.name: Eliminate
qed/part.uPattern.desc: Finds \mark{meta-all}x. ?P(x) \mark{dot-equals} t where ?P is applied to distinct variables bound by the \mark{meta-all} and t contains no other \mark{meta-all} variable, and solves ?P \mark{dot-equals} fun x => t. When ?P is applied to anything else (?P(ann), ?P(?t)), the equation is left unchanged.
qed/part.uPattern.name: Pattern unification
qed/part.uSwap.desc: Finds an equation with a ?-letter on the right only, t \mark{dot-equals} ?A, and turns it into ?A \mark{dot-equals} t.
qed/part.uSwap.name: Orient
qed/part.unifier.desc: Solves a set of equations to the end: each with a ?-letter on the left and none of those letters on any right side (the most general unifier); reports failure if there is none.
qed/part.unifier.name: Unifier
qed/part.unifier.revisions.0.desc: Solves a set of equations to the end: each with a ?-letter on the left and none of those letters on any right side (the most general unifier); reports failure if there is none. An equation like ?P(x) is not solved but left as it is.
